program_name: Quantitative and Computational Biology (QCB) - Master's Degree / Laurea Magistrale in Biologia Quantitativa e Computazionale
teaching_language: Fully English. The programme page states 'LANGUAGE: English' and 'The programme is fully taught in English', and Art. 1 c.2 of the binding Italian call states 'La lingua ufficiale del corso di studio e l'inglese' ('The official language of the course is English'). There is no Italian-language percorso and no mixed English/Italian track: both curricula (Computational and Quantitative) are delivered entirely in English. The first-year plan additionally contains a compulsory 3 CFU 'English C1' unit, which confirms the English-medium nature of the degree. Note that the programme is officially registered in Italian under the name 'Biologia Quantitativa e Computazionale' - the Italian name appears on all binding legal documents (rectoral decree, bando, regolamento didattico) but does not indicate any Italian-taught teaching.
campus: Trento - Povo campus. Department of Cellular, Computational and Integrative Biology (CIBIO), Via Sommarive 9, 38123 Povo (Trento), inside the 'Fabio Ferrari' Scientific and Technological Hub, Povo 2 building (department offices on floor -1). Some teaching units of the two curricula are delivered by the Departments of Physics, Mathematics and Information Engineering and Computer Science (DISI) on the neighbouring Povo / Polo Ferrari premises (Via Sommarive 5 and Via Sommarive 14). Lessons take place only in person; the Student Support Service and International Mobility Office for CIBIO students are at Polo Ferrari 1, Via Sommarive 5, 38123 Povo (TN).
degree_class: LM-8 R (Biotecnologie industriali / Industrial Biotechnology). The binding Italian call (amended version, Rectoral Decree annex of 30 April 2026) is headed 'Bando per l'ammissione al corso di laurea magistrale in Biologia Quantitativa e Computazionale - Classe di laurea LM-8 R'. The 'R' suffix indicates the renewed degree class introduced by the Italian ministerial reform of degree classes. Duration 2 years, 120 ECTS, course code 0525H in the UniTrento/CINECA course catalogue.
admission_type: RESTRICTED ACCESS (numero programmato / 'ACCESS: Programmed' on the official programme page). This is NOT an open-access programme. Admission is by a public selection based on qualifications and, where necessary, an interview ('selezione pubblica per titoli ed eventuale colloquio'). Total intake for a.y. 2026/2027: 45 places, of which 4 are reserved for non-European citizens living outside Italy and the remaining 41 are for Europeans and equivalents. The selection is organised in two separate sessions with two separate ranking lists: Session I (non-Europeans only, deadline 23 March 2026) and Session II (Europeans and equivalents only, deadline in summer 2026). Any places not assigned in Session I are transferred to Session II. There is NO TOLC, NO SAT and no written entrance examination; scoring is entirely document-based (up to 100 points) with an optional interview requested by the Committee only when the submitted documents are insufficient for evaluation. Eligibility threshold: 50/100.
academic_requirements:
SEATS AND QUOTAS (a.y. 2026/2027): 45 places in total, including a reserved quota of 4 places for non-European citizens not resident in Italy; 41 places for Europeans and equivalents. Unassigned non-EU places roll over to the second (European) session. The published non-EU ranking for 2026/2027 lists 4 admitted candidates (top score 99.07/100, fourth admitted score 92.125/100), 20 candidates on the waiting list and 7 declared not eligible, and 1 scholarship available.

DEGREE REQUIREMENT (identical for both categories): a Bachelor's or first-level degree of at least 3 years awarded in Italy or abroad and recognised as equivalent and suitable.

CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (as amended on 30 April 2026 following observations of the National University Council - CUN; these amended requirements are the operative ones):
(a) Applicants holding an Italian Bachelor's degree in class L-2 Biotechnologies (or class 1 Biotecnologie under the previous D.M. 509/99) automatically meet the curricular requirements.
(b) Applicants holding an Italian degree in a class other than L-2 must have in their study path at least: 12 ECTS in the SSD BIO/09 Physiology, BIO/10 Biochemistry, BIO/11 Molecular biology, BIO/13 Experimental biology, BIO/18 Genetics; AND at least 6 ECTS in CHIM/01 Analytical chemistry, CHIM/03 General and inorganic chemistry, CHIM/06 Organic chemistry; AND at least 6 ECTS in MAT/03 Geometry, MAT/05 Mathematical analysis, MAT/06 Probability and statistics, SECS-S/01 Statistics, SECS-S/02 Statistics for experimental and technological research; AND at least 6 ECTS in FIS/01 Experimental physics, FIS/02 Theoretical physics/mathematical models and methods, FIS/03 Physics of matter, FIS/07 Applied physics.
(c) Applicants with a degree obtained abroad, or under a system that does not use ECTS/SSD, are assessed by evaluating the consistency of the contents and learning outcomes of the courses taken against the disciplinary sectors listed above.

GRADUATION DEADLINES: final-year students may apply, provided the Bachelor's degree is obtained by 30 June 2026 for non-European citizens, or by 31 October 2026 for Europeans and equivalents (and for non-Europeans who graduate at an Italian university and hold a valid Italian study residence permit). At the end of the admission/enrolment process, any unassigned places may be given to eligible European/equivalent candidates in the ranking who did not meet the requirements by 31 October 2026, provided all requirements are met by the final enrolment date.

SELECTION AND SCORING (Art. 4 of the call, out of 100 points): (a) coherence between the candidate's previous qualification and the objectives of the Master's in Quantitative and Computational Biology - max 40 points; (b) curriculum studiorum (credit-weighted average of examinations taken excluding the final exam, thesis topic, performance and evaluations obtained in previous studies, any post-graduate qualifications, other training activities; personal preparation is additionally verified in the interview if one is held) - max 40 points; (c) personal written statement of purpose (max 500 words) plus further language competences and any other certifications - max 20 points. The English version of the call additionally mentions a 'video presentation' under item (c), evaluated only if a minimum combined score is reached on items (a) and (b) [uncertain - the binding Italian text does not mention a video]. Candidates scoring 50/100 or more are declared eligible; in case of a tie, priority goes to the younger candidate. The Committee is appointed by rectoral decree and consists of at least 3 professors of the CIBIO Department (three members according to the English version); it may meet by video conference. If the submitted documents do not allow an adequate evaluation, the candidate may be asked to supply further documentation (e.g. syllabi of examinations taken) and/or to sit an interview in person or by conference call. Two distinct ranking lists are drawn up (non-EU and EU/equivalents) and published on the programme webpage.

FEES AND SCHOLARSHIPS FOR NON-EU STUDENTS: maximum annual tuition EUR 10,000 for non-EU citizens living abroad, reduced according to the admission score - full tuition waiver for 90-100/100, EUR 1,000 for 70-89.99/100, EUR 3,000 for 60-69.99/100, EUR 6,500 for 50-59.99/100. Second-year fees depend on credits earned by 10 August 2027: full waiver for 42 or more ECTS, EUR 1,000 for 36-41, EUR 3,000 for 24-35, EUR 6,500 for 6-23, EUR 10,000 for fewer than 6. Scholarships: non-European candidates at the top of the ranking scoring at least 70/100 may be awarded a scholarship; 1 scholarship was available for 2026/2027; no separate application is needed, holders are exempt from tuition fees, the scholarship is a partial contribution to living costs paid only after actual arrival in Italy, may be renewed for the second year subject to merit requirements, and is not compatible with MAECI, Universita a colori-Unicolor or Invest your Talent in Italy scholarships. For Europeans and equivalents, tuition is income-based (ISEE) and can be partially or fully reduced.

SECOND-YEAR ADMISSION: candidates who have already passed first-year examinations of this Master's degree, or equivalent courses in previous academic careers at other universities, may apply for admission to the second year, subject to availability of places and to the programme's Guidelines for degree programme changes, transfers and second-year admission; applications open from May 2026. If second-year admission is refused, the applicant may still be admitted to the first year only if they applied under the current call and were ranked eligible.
language_requirements:
English at CEFR level B2 (full B2 level, four skills) is mandatory for all applicants. There is no Italian language requirement for admission, as the programme is entirely English-taught. The level must be documented by the deadline of the session in which the candidate applies (23 March 2026 for non-Europeans; the Session II deadline for Europeans and equivalents).

Accepted proofs: (a) a certificate issued by an internationally recognised body; (b) a certificate attesting the required level issued by a certifying body or a university institution (self-certification under arts. 46-47 of D.P.R. 445/2000 is allowed when the issuing body is an Italian public institution); (c) a statement issued by the institution that awarded the first- or second-cycle degree certifying that the official teaching language of the completed programme was English; (d) an online declaration of holding the citizenship of a country whose official language is English (the corsi.unitn.it webpage also accepts a self-declaration of having graduated in an English-speaking country); (e) an online declaration of having passed an English language examination at least at B2 level during the Bachelor's degree, provided all four language skills were assessed and the language exam appears as passed in the transcript.

GRACE PERIOD: candidates applying in Session II (Europeans and equivalents) who cannot certify the required English level at the application deadline are still admitted to the selection, but must produce the final language certification by 31 October 2026.

MAKE-UP TEST: applicants (Europeans and equivalents route) who hold none of the above can make up the requirement by taking and passing the English test at the University Language Centre (Centro Linguistico di Ateneo, CLA) before enrolment. The written part is held in person in Trento at the CLA and the speaking part is online. Five CLA sessions were published for Master's degree admission in 2026 - Session 1: registration 27 March to 20 April 12:00, written 27 April 14:30, speaking 8 May; Session 2: registration 20 April to 15 May 12:00, written 25 May 14:30, speaking 5 June; Session 3: registration 16 May to 25 June 12:00, written 6 July 14:30, speaking 17 July; Session 4: registration 26 June to 21 August 12:00, written 2 September 14:30, speaking 11 September; Session 5: registration 24 August to 2 October 12:00, written 12 October 14:30, speaking 23 October. Once the language requirement is achieved the candidate must email the Admission office to proceed with enrolment. Registration for the CLA test is made through https://webapps.unitn.it/Apply/en/Web/GoHome/ammissione/ENAdm_STA26 . Note that the study plan also includes a compulsory 3 CFU 'English C1' course during the first year, so a higher level is expected to be reached during the degree.
required_documents:
The same document list applies to both the non-EU (Session I) and the EU/equivalents (Session II) online applications. An official translation into English or Italian is required for any document not originally issued in one of those two languages. Illegible documents are not considered and incomplete or unsubmitted application forms are excluded from the selection.

1. A copy of a valid passport (non-EU citizens: personal-data pages with photo only) or identity card (EU citizens); not required for applicants logging in with an Italian digital identity.
2. Curriculum vitae et studiorum in English, following the European/Europass format (https://europass.europa.eu/en).
3. A copy of the Bachelor's degree certificate, or a certificate of enrolment stating the expected graduation date. Graduates of Italian public universities submit a self-declaration under arts. 46-47 of D.P.R. 445/2000; UniTrento students/graduates do not need to upload this document.
4. A copy of the transcript of academic records including the complete list of examinations (final-year students must also list examinations not yet passed), the Scientific Disciplinary Sectors (SSD) - only for degrees obtained at an Italian university - the marks obtained, and, for degrees obtained abroad, the weighted average mark and the minimum-to-maximum range of marks. Same self-declaration rule as above for Italian public universities.
5. A statement of purpose / short personal essay written in English (max 1 page in the English version of the call; max 500 words for scoring purposes) describing the candidate's interests and expectations regarding the learning objectives of the Master's degree.
6. Proof of English proficiency at B2 level (certificate or substitutive declaration as described in the language requirements).

An application fee of EUR 30.00 must be paid by the deadline of each session; failure to pay results in exclusion from the selection. Login to the online application system ('Degree Courses in English Application') is possible via SPID digital identity, electronic identity card (CIE), a @unitn.it username, or a temporary @guest.unitn.it username (which should be created at least 48 hours before the deadline). Admitted candidates then pay a non-refundable enrolment confirmation fee of EUR 100.00 (Europeans and equivalents admitted in the second session are exempt from this fee if they complete enrolment within 7 days of the admission notice). Non-European admitted candidates must additionally pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal at the competent Italian diplomatic representation and obtain a study visa; pre-enrolment is mandatory to receive the UniTrento admission letter. UniTrento may request a statement of verification and/or statement of comparability for foreign qualifications; the eligibility of a foreign degree is verified only after the admission and pre-enrolment procedure is complete.
entry_exam_or_test: No entrance examination. There is no TOLC, no SAT and no written admission test for this programme - selection is by evaluation of qualifications only (documents scored out of 100 points). An INTERVIEW is not a standard step: it is held in person or by conference call only when the documents attached to the online application do not allow the Admissions Committee to evaluate the candidature adequately, in which case the Committee may also request further documentation such as the syllabi of examinations taken. The English courtesy translation of the call additionally refers to an optional video presentation as part of the third scoring criterion, evaluated only if a minimum combined score is reached on the first two criteria [uncertain - not present in the binding Italian text]. The only test any applicant may have to sit is the English language test at the Centro Linguistico di Ateneo (CLA), and only for candidates who cannot otherwise document B2 English.

uncertainty_notes:
1) THE TASK NOTE 'Serbest erisim' (open/free access) IS WRONG. This programme is NOT open access. The official programme page states 'ACCESS: Programmed' (numero programmato) and Art. 1 of the binding call describes 'una selezione pubblica' restricted to 45 places (4 reserved for non-EU citizens abroad, 41 for Europeans and equivalents). Applicants must pass a document-based competitive selection scored out of 100 with a 50/100 eligibility threshold, and even eligible candidates can end up on a waiting list (20 non-EU candidates were waitlisted for 2026/2027). This record should be treated as correcting the source list.

2) EU/EQUIVALENTS DEADLINE - TWO CONFLICTING OFFICIAL DATES. The binding Italian call and its 30 April 2026 amendment both state Session II runs 'a partire dal 21 aprile 2026 ed entro le ore 12.00 del 30 giugno 2026'. The live programme webpage (last published 30 July 2026) instead states the application window is '30 April to 6 July 2026 at 12:00 CET' and repeats 'Deadline: 6 July 2026 at 12:00 CET'. The webpage is more recent and is what applicants actually saw, so 6 July 2026 is reported as the operative date, but no rectifying decree confirming the extension was found on corsi.unitn.it. Field marked uncertain.

3) THE ENGLISH COURTESY TRANSLATION OF THE CALL IS UNRELIABLE AND PARTLY SUPERSEDED. (a) It is explicitly labelled non-binding and 'produced with the support of AI-assisted tools'. (b) Its Art. 2 B and Art. 4 c.1 both give the application deadline as '4 March 2026' / 'March 4, 2026 at 12.00', which matches no session of this call and appears to be copied from another UniTrento call - the real Session I deadline is 23 March 2026. (c) Its curricular requirements are the ORIGINAL February 2026 ones (12 CFU across a combined BIO+CHIM list of which at least 6 CFU in BIO, plus 12 CFU across a combined MAT/FIS/SECS-S list) and were superseded by the 30 April 2026 amendment, which splits them into 12 BIO + 6 CHIM + 6 MAT/statistics + 6 FIS and narrows the SSD lists. Anyone relying on the English PDF alone would be misinformed on both points. The amended requirements reported here match both the binding rettifica and the current webpage.

4) VIDEO PRESENTATION - ENGLISH-ONLY ELEMENT. The English translation lists 'video presentation' among the elements scored under criterion (c) (max 20 points), with a footnote explaining it is evaluated only if a minimum combined score is reached on criteria (a) and (b). The binding Italian text of both the original call and the rettifica mentions only the written statement, further language competences and other certifications. It is therefore unclear whether a video was actually requested; no video upload appears in the document list of either version. Marked uncertain in the entry_exam_or_test and academic_requirements fields.

5) COMMITTEE SIZE - minor discrepancy: the English version says 'The Admissions Committee is made up of three members', the binding Italian says 'si compone di almeno 3 docenti del Dipartimento Biologia Cellulare, Computazionale e Integrata' (at least three professors of CIBIO). The Italian 'at least three' prevails.

6) WAF/ACCESS LIMITATION. corsi.unitn.it, www.unitn.it and offertaformativa.unitn.it sit behind an AWS WAF/Cloudflare layer that returns HTTP 405 (with x-amzn-waf-action: captcha) or 503 on direct fetches; the CAPTCHA was deliberately not bypassed. All corsi.unitn.it webpages and PDFs above were retrieved through a public read-only text-extraction proxy that renders the same public pages, so the content is the live official text but was not read from a direct browser session. offertaformativa.unitn.it now returns a 'Site under maintenance' notice redirecting to www.unitn.it/en/study/courses, so any programme data still indexed by search engines under offertaformativa.unitn.it (e.g. the widely cached '30 April to 30 June' application window) is from a retired site and was not used. webapps.unitn.it was reached directly: the EU application endpoint QuCoBi2026EU returns HTTP 200 and is live but login-gated, so in-portal dates could not be cross-checked; no non-EU application endpoint is linked any more because that session is closed.

7) INTERDEPARTMENTAL NATURE. The task note describes the programme as 'CIBIO + Fisica + Matematica + DISI'. Administratively the degree belongs solely to the Department of Cellular, Computational and Integrative Biology (CIBIO) - the call, the Committee and the admission office are all CIBIO/Science-and-Technology-Area. The involvement of the Departments of Physics, Mathematics and DISI is at teaching level: the study plan draws courses such as Quantum mechanics, Regression and Classification Models, Machine learning, Knowledge Graphs and Bio-Inspired Artificial Intelligence from those departments. There is no inter-university (interateneo) agreement and no double-degree partnership documented for this programme.

8) CYCLE ALREADY CONCLUDED. As of the research date (31 August 2026) both 2026/2027 sessions are closed: the non-EU application closed on 23 March 2026 and its ranking was published on 14 May 2026; the EU/equivalents session closed in summer 2026. Applicants targeting the next intake should expect an equivalent call to be published around December 2025-February 2026 equivalent timing, i.e. early 2027 for a.y. 2027/2028.

9) NAMING. The programme is not new (teaching regulations exist from 2016 onwards) but was substantially redesigned for 2026/2027: the amended cohort plan introduces the two curricula 'Computational' and 'Quantitative' and new courses such as AI Techniques for Data Analysis and Multiscale RNA and Protein Omics. Historic documents on the programme site are filed under the Italian name 'Biologia Quantitativa e Computazionale'; the English name 'Quantitative and Computational Biology' is the one used for all English-language materials. The English call PDF contains the typo 'Quantitative and Cmputational Biology'.

10) CAMPUS ADDRESS. The official programme page gives only 'LOCATION: Cellular, Computational and Integrative Biology - CIBIO' without a street address. The address Via Sommarive 9, 38123 Povo (Trento), Povo 2 building of the 'Fabio Ferrari' Scientific and Technological Hub, comes from the CIBIO department site (cibio.unitn.it) and from the UniTrento locations page, not from the programme page itself; the Povo/Trento location is certain.
